chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn al-Numan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Shayba al-Zuhri, from Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him) who said:

The worst of servants is a servant who has two faces and two tongues. He commends his brother in his presence and devours him in his absence. If he is given [a blessing], he envies him, and if he is afflicted, he abandons him.

key_terms.ذا لسانين: Two-tongued: speaking differently depending on whether one is present or absent
key_terms.ذا وجهين: Two-faced: possessing two faces, a metaphor for hypocrisy and duplicity in social interactions
key_terms.يأكله: Devours him: a metaphor for backbiting (ghiba), consuming someone's honor through gossip
key_terms.يطري: To commend extravagantly, to flatter with excessive praise

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about two-faced and two-tongued people?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) condemns the two-faced person who flatters others in person but backbites them in their absence, and who is driven by envy in good times and abandonment in difficult times. This teaching was delivered in the context of early Muslim community ethics, where hypocrisy and duplicity were seen as spiritually destructive vices that undermine social trust and brotherhood.
word_analysis: al-Baqir (the one who splits open knowledge)

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. `Ali Majiluwayh (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-`Attar narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi’l Khattab narrated to us from al-Hasan b. `Ali b. Faddal from `Ali b. al-Nu`man from `Abdullah b. Muskan from Dawud b. Farqad from Abi Shayba al-Zuhri from Abi Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali al-Baqir (as). He said:

The worst of worshipers is a worshiper with two faces and two tongues. He commends his brother when he is around, and he consumes him [in gossip] when he is absent. When he is given, he envies, and when he suffers, he lets him down.
